editorial:
If you grew up watching the Ben 10 cartoon, this live-action TV movie feels like a fun trip back to your childhood. You follow Ben, Gwen, and Grandpa Max as they try to stop an alien villain named Eon from opening a gateway that would let an army of aliens invade Earth. The story moves quickly, mixing action scenes with light humor and family-friendly moments. The Omnitrix transformations look surprisingly good for a TV movie, and the young cast brings enough energy to keep you entertained. It is not a big-budget blockbuster, but it does not need to be. The movie knows exactly what it is and delivers a solid adventure for fans of the franchise.

On the plus side, the pacing rarely drags, and the action sequences are easy to follow. The villain has a clear goal, which keeps the story focused. On the downside, some of the dialogue feels a bit cheesy, and a few effects look dated. Still, if you are looking for a fun family movie night pick, this one works well. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection. It is a great choice for kids and nostalgic fans alike.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ben confronts Eon at the gateway site. Eon tries to open the portal to bring his alien army through, but Ben uses the Omnitrix to transform into powerful aliens and fight him off. With help from Gwen and Max, Ben manages to destroy the gateway and stop the invasion. Eon is defeated and sent back through the portal, which closes for good. The movie ends with Ben, Gwen, and Max celebrating their victory and heading off on their next adventure together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family adventure movies and the Ben 10 franchise.
